items.title: Waymo to bring autonomous ride-hailing to Las Vegas
items.topic: Waymo to bring autonomous ride-hailing to Las Vegas
items.summary: Waymo is expanding its autonomous ride-hailing service to Las Vegas, marking a significant step in the company's efforts to deploy self-driving vehicles in new urban environments. The deployment will leverage Waymo's advanced AV technology, which has been tested and refined in multiple cities, to provide a safe and reliable transportation option for residents and visitors.

items.title: Tesla’s record month: 4 fatal Autopilot and Full Self-Driving crashes
items.topic: Tesla’s record month: 4 fatal Autopilot and Full Self-Driving crashes
items.summary: Tesla experienced a record month with four fatal crashes involving its Autopilot and Full Self-Driving (FSD) systems, raising serious concerns about the safety and reliability of these technologies. The incidents have prompted increased scrutiny from regulators and the public, highlighting the need for more rigorous testing and oversight in the development of autonomous driving systems.

items.title: Inside Rivian’s Bid to Build Level 4 Robotaxis—and Then Passenger Cars
items.topic: Inside Rivian’s Bid to Build Level 4 Robotaxis—and Then Passenger Cars
items.summary: Rivian is developing Level 4 robotaxis, aiming to build fully autonomous vehicles that can operate without human intervention. The company's strategy involves leveraging advanced sensor fusion and computer vision technologies to achieve this goal, with plans to eventually transition to producing passenger cars. This initiative underscores Rivian's commitment to advancing the state of autonomous vehicle technology.

items.title: US agency orders Tesla to answer questions on Cybercab certification
items.topic: US agency orders Tesla to answer questions on Cybercab certification
items.summary: The National Highway Traffic Safety Administration (NHTSA) has ordered Tesla to provide detailed information on the certification of its Cybercab, a new electric vehicle designed for autonomous ride-hailing. The agency's request comes amid growing concerns about the safety and regulatory compliance of Tesla's autonomous driving technologies.

items.title: OpenAI pushes for mandatory national AI safety rules
items.topic: OpenAI pushes for mandatory national AI safety rules
items.summary: OpenAI is advocating for the implementation of mandatory national AI safety rules, emphasizing the need for standardized regulations to ensure the responsible development and deployment of AI technologies. This push for regulation reflects growing concerns about the potential risks and ethical implications of advanced AI systems.

items.topic: OpenAI, Anthropic, Google have been in talks on AI safety for weeks
items.summary: OpenAI, Anthropic, and Google have been engaged in ongoing discussions about AI safety, focusing on collaborative efforts to address the ethical and technical challenges associated with advanced AI systems. items.title: OpenAI Reveals More Instances Of Concerning AI Model Behaviors During Testing
items.topic: OpenAI Reveals More Instances Of Concerning AI Model Behaviors During Testing
items.summary: OpenAI has disclosed additional instances of concerning behaviors exhibited by its AI models during testing, raising questions about the robustness and reliability of these systems. The findings underscore the ongoing challenges in ensuring that AI models operate safely and predictably, particularly in real-world applications.

items.title: Adaptive stress testing of autonomous vehicle-pedestrian interactions: A large language model (LLM) distillation approach
items.topic: Adaptive stress testing of autonomous vehicle-pedestrian interactions: A large language model (LLM) distillation approach
items.source: Transportation Research Part C: Emerging Technologies
items.summary: Xiao Wen, Wentao Huang, Zhiyong Cui, and Sisi Jian from Transportation Research Part C: Emerging Technologies used a large language model (LLM) to distill and adaptively test autonomous vehicle-pedestrian interactions. The study, published in January 2027, demonstrates how LLMs can enhance the testing and safety of AVs by simulating complex pedestrian scenarios, improving the robustness of AV systems.

items.title: Accurate and sample efficient driver takeover time prediction in autonomous driving with privacy preservation: A federated meta attentive interpretable tabular learning approach
items.topic: Accurate and sample efficient driver takeover time prediction in autonomous driving with privacy preservation: A federated meta attentive interpretable tabular learning approach
items.source: Transportation Research Part C: Emerging Technologies
items.summary: Weida Yang, Zhizhou Wu, Yinhai Wang, and Yunyi Liang from Transportation Research Part C: Emerging Technologies developed a federated meta attentive interpretable tabular learning approach to predict driver takeover time in autonomous driving. Published in December 2026, the study achieves accurate and sample-efficient predictions while preserving privacy, enhancing the interpretability and reliability of AV systems.

items.title: How do emotional cues influence drivers' pre-takeover readiness in automated driving? Evidence from olfaction-involved affective multimodal interaction
items.topic: How do emotional cues influence drivers' pre-takeover readiness in automated driving? Evidence from olfaction-involved affective multimodal interaction
items.source: Transportation Research Part F: Traffic Psychology and Behaviour
items.summary: Yinjie Lv, Chunhui Jing, Guanyu Lei, and Teng Zhao from Transportation Research Part F: Traffic Psychology and Behaviour investigated how emotional cues, particularly olfactory stimuli, influence drivers' pre-takeover readiness in automated driving. Published in August 2026, the study provides insights into the affective multimodal interactions that can improve driver engagement and trust in AVs.
